record.original_question: Which geometric properties of the domain do uniform estimates depend on? [e.g.L2 estimates depend on the diameter and the dimension ].

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4.2 Which geometric properties of the domain do uniform estimates depend on? [e.g.L2 estimates depend on the diameter and the dimension ].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded pseudoconvex domain. Consider the inhomogeneous Cauchy–Riemann equation $\bar\partial u = f$, where $f$ is a $\bar\partial$-closed $(0,1)$-form on $\Omega$ with bounded coefficients. It is classical that on every such $\Omega$ there exists a (canonical) $L^2$ solution $u$ satisfying $\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C \|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$, where the constant $C$ depends only on the diameter of $\Omega$ and the complex dimension $n$. By contrast, uniform ($L^\infty$) estimates of the form $\|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \le C \|f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}$ are known to fail for general bounded pseudoconvex domains, while they hold on strictly pseudoconvex domains and on certain piecewise smooth strictly pseudoconvex domains.

Determine, in a precise quantitative form, on which geometric invariants of the domain $\Omega$ uniform estimates for solutions of $\bar\partial u = f$ depend. That is, identify a set of geometric quantities $G_1(\Omega), G_2(\Omega), \dots$ (such as boundary regularity, type, Levi geometry, peak-function data, etc.) such that there exists a solution $u$ to $\bar\partial u = f$ with $\|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \le C(G_1(\Omega), \dots, G_k(\Omega)) \|f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}$ for every bounded $\bar\partial$-closed $(0,1)$-form $f$, and characterize the dependence as sharply as possible (in analogy to the $L^2$ case, where dependence is on the diameter and the dimension).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of which geometric properties of a domain control uniform ($L^\infty$) estimates for the $\bar\partial$-equation remains a central open problem in several complex variables. Recent work (e.g., on obstructions to uniform estimates and on Kerzman's question, including a 2025 paper in Peking Mathematical Journal) continues to address partial cases—strictly pseudoconvex domains, piecewise smooth domains, product domains, convex domains of finite type—but no general characterization of the geometric invariants governing uniform estimates is known. Fornæss–Sibony's counterexample shows that smoothness and pseudoconvexity alone do not suffice.

status_evidence.title: Obstructions to uniform estimates for solutions to the d-bar equation
status_evidence.snippet: Each boundary point must admit a peak function; geometrical obstructions to uniform estimates for the d-bar equation are examined.
status_evidence.claim: The geometric conditions on a pseudoconvex domain ensuring uniform $\bar\partial$ estimates remain only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: Uniform Estimates of the Cauchy–Riemann Equation and Kerzman's Question
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continues to investigate uniform estimates and Kerzman's question on general pseudoconvex domains.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is still actively pursued, with no complete characterization.

status_evidence.title: Uniform estimates for the canonical solution to the ∂̄-equation on product domains
status_evidence.snippet: Uniform estimates fail on general pseudoconvex domains (Fornæss–Sibony counterexample) while they hold in special geometries like product domains.
status_evidence.claim: General dependence of uniform estimates on geometry is unresolved.
